sentence: This project studies how diabetes changes the nerve signals that reach the heart in rats, and whether activating a small group of neurons can slow the damage.
This project builds statistical methods that use genetic scores and family-based studies to help explain what causes complex human diseases.
This project tries to find out why many patients with lymphoma relapse after immunotherapy, and which biomarkers can predict it.
This project tests lipid nanoparticles that deliver gene-editing tools to blood stem cells as a way to treat inherited blood disorders.
This project uses wearables and smartphone-based sensors to study how emotion regulation problems lead to suicidal ideation in people at clinical high risk for psychosis.
This project builds 3D models from endoscopy videos by modeling how light reflects from mucus layers and how organs deform over time.
This project tries to find out how Mycobacteria move lipids to build their outer membrane.
This project studies how retinal ganglion cells develop and how they might be regrown from dormant progenitor cells in the adult retina.
This project shares research on how axons and dendrites form and how neurons connect with each other.
This project builds a computational approach that uses clinical reports to predict whether a genetic variant is likely to cause disease.
This project tries to find out how weight loss slows the progression of knee osteoarthritis in overweight and obese people.
This project builds models of Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome and Valley Fever to study hosts as disease reservoirs and improve forecasting.
This project studies a pattern of brain activity linked to mood and anxiety, and how it affects behavior in mice.
This project builds a portable positron emission tomography scanner for brain imaging that can work alone or with MRI systems.
This project builds a technology that uses a blood sample and artificial intelligence to find very low levels of tumor.
This project builds sequencing and visualization tools to find which genes are read to make which proteins in aging breast tissues and breast tumors.
This project tries to find out which regulators control a pathway that watches over mitochondria, and how they affect host survival during infection.
This project studies how the nervous system balances small, fast active sensing movements with goal-directed control.
This project studies the circuit mechanisms that let the auditory system adapt to everyday listening situations.
This project looks for pairs of drugs that together eliminate the antibiotic-resistant pathogen Acinetobacter baumannii, using chemical synthetic lethality.
